extracted.intended_audience: NIH R01 applicants, grant reviewers, and research teams preparing biomedical R01 proposals (NIAID/NIH context)
extracted.subtask_description: A peer review summary statement for an NIH R01 (NIAID) application describing reviewer evaluations across standard NIH review criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) plus human/animal subject protections, inclusion, resource sharing, and scoring notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (Impact Score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: General summary judgment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field. Example summary: "Overall, the review committee expressed an exceptional level of enthusiasm for this application."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative should summarize strengths and weaknesses and state overall enthusiasm. Impact/priority score is calculated by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers and multiplying by 10. Percentile ranking may also be provided. Reviewer criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting and are not discussed or calculated into the overall impact score at the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? Example: "This application advances a theory of pre-existing immunity against S. aureus as a cause of vaccine failure..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess public health importance (e.g., SA as a leading pathogen), whether the work would move the field forward, and whether preliminary data support the rationale. Strengths and weaknesses include presence/absence of convincing preliminary data, potential limitations (e.g., duration of protective serum responses waning by 6 months), and relevance of model systems to human disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? Example: "Dr. Liu is an expert... Dr. Creech is an expert in clinical S. aureus infection. The MPI plan is acceptable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes expertise, productivity, complementary skills, multi-PI (MPI) arrangements, and consultant support (e.g., biostatistics). Weaknesses can include limited prior collaboration among PIs and minor concerns about team integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms? Example: "Conceptual innovation in studying pre-existing antibody interference... Targeting subdominant S. aureus antigens for vaccine design is of interest."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate novelty of concepts, models, or approaches and whether prior publications by the PI(s) partially overlap (may undercut novelty). Note both conceptual and technical innovations (e.g., new human serum transfer mouse model).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the aims? Example: "Research plan is rigorous with adequate statistical analysis and experimental replicates. Anticipated results, pitfalls and alternative approaches are thoroughly considered."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers examine study design rigor, power/replication, statistical analysis plans, predefined cut-offs, consideration of pitfalls/alternatives, logistics (e.g., sample volume planning), and whether aims are interdependent. Weaknesses noted: lack of discussion of sources for healthy controls, minor grantsmanship (figure layout), and limited depth in some immunology/memory-recall analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment contribute to the probability of success? Example: "The research environments at UCSD and Vanderbilt are excellent. All relevant cores are present."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess institutional support, availability of necessary facilities and cores, collaborative environment, and potential logistical issues (e.g., physical separation of teams).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Are human subjects protections adequate and risks acceptable? Example: "They will recruit 75 kids and 25 older adults with invasive S. aureus infections and sample up to 20ml of blood at 3-4 time points post infection."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review assesses recruitment procedures, informed consent, risk/benefit, sampling volumes/timepoints, monitoring, and whether protections are acceptable. Page notes "Acceptable Risks and/or Adequate Protections."

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Plans (sex/gender, race/ethnicity, age)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are plans for inclusion of sexes/genders, racial/ethnic groups, and age ranges justified scientifically? Example: "Sex/Gender: Distribution justified scientifically. Race/Ethnicity: Distribution justified scientifically. Inclusion/Exclusion Based on Age: Distribution justified scientifically."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect a justified strategy for inclusion, sampling plans across the lifespan, and explanation of how these variables will be incorporated into analysis. Specific reviewer comments sometimes request more detail on how age will affect antibody responses or be included analytically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH-specific assessment of plans to include women in the study. SRO summary status: "ACCEPTABLE."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must justify representation and show how sex/gender will be addressed; reviewers mark as acceptable/not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Minorities Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH-specific assessment of plans to include racial and ethnic minorities. SRO summary status: "ACCEPTABLE."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must justify representation of minority groups and scientific rationale; reviewers report acceptance status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Across the Lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH-specific assessment of inclusion of appropriate age groups (children, adults, older adults). SRO summary status: "ACCEPTABLE."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires justification for age distribution and plans for recruitment/analysis across lifespan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex as a Biological Variable (SABV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of sex as a biological variable in experimental design and sampling. Example mentions: "Sex as a biological variable is appropriately addressed" and use of male and female human samples and animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether both sexes are included where appropriate and whether analyses will consider sex-specific effects. Not addressing SABV can be a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the vertebrate animals' use and welfare adequately addressed? Example: At one point the document flags lack of adequate discussion of monitoring pain/distress and euthanasia criteria; in other critiques the section is noted as "YES, all criteria addressed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect explicit descriptions of animal welfare monitoring, criteria for euthanasia, rationales for animal models, and that all animal care issues are addressed. Deficiencies here are noted as weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Are biohazard issues and containment appropriate? Example: "S. aureus and human blood are BSL2. Biohazards: Acceptable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess biosafety level justification, facility capability, and whether protocols minimize risk. Status often reported as Acceptable/Unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for sharing data, model organisms, or other resources. SRO summary: "Acceptable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review evaluates whether resource sharing plans (data, reagents, protocols) are adequate and realistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans to authenticate/validate key reagents and biological resources. SRO summary: "Acceptable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for methods to authenticate cell lines, reagents, antibodies, and other critical materials to ensure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the budget reasonable and justified for the proposed work? Example: "Budget and Period of Support: Recommend as Requested."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review includes evaluation of cost realism and whether requested resources match proposed activities. Committee may recommend full funding as requested or adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-PI (MPI) Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the multi-principal investigator leadership plan. Example: "The MPI plan is acceptable/well laid out."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity of roles, complementary expertise, communication plan, and how leadership responsibilities are shared. Lack of prior collaboration among PIs can be noted as a minor weakness unless mitigated by consultants or plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and Review Process Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural information about how scores are collected and calculated. Example: "The criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers assigned to an application, and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. The impact/priority score is calculated..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that individual criterion scores are provided pre-meeting, overall impact score is given after discussion and computed across voting reviewers, and percentile rankings may be provided. Also points reviewers/applicants to NIH resources and next steps (e.g., https://grants.nih.gov/grants/next_steps.htm and peer review process links).
